nodes.text: Let $f(k)$ be the maximal value of $n_1$ such that there exist $n_1<n_2<\cdots <n_k$ with\[1=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}.\]Is it true that\[f(k)=(1+o(1))\frac{k}{e-1}?\]

#284 : [ErGr80] number theory | unit fractions The upper bound $f(k) \leq (1+o(1))\frac{k}{e-1}$ is trivial since for any $u\geq 1$ we have\[\sum_{u\leq n\leq eu}\frac{1}{n}=1+o(1),\]and hence if $f(k)=u$ then we must have $k\geq (e-1-o(1))u$. Essentially solved by Croot [Cr01] , who showed that for any $N>1$ there exists some $k\geq 1$ and\[N<n_1<\cdots <n_k \leq (e+o(1))N\]with $1=\sum \frac{1}{n_i}$.
